latest.content:
Today 10:01
Annual Financial Report and Notice of Annual General Meeting
27 August 2026
Mothercare plc ("the Company")
NOTICE OF AGM AND POSTING OF ANNUAL REPORT
Mothercare plc has posted its Annual Report and Accounts for the year ended 28 March 2026 together with its Notice of Annual General Meeting (“AGM”).
The AGM will be held at 11.00am on 24 September 2026 at the offices of Bird & Bird LLP, 12 New Fetter Lane, London, EC4A 1JP.
Shareholders are encouraged to submit their proxy votes ahead of the meeting and appoint the chair of the AGM as their proxy. Shareholders are also invited to send questions relating to the business of the meeting by email to: investorrelations@mothercare.com to be received by 11.00 am on 22 September 2026.
Copies of both the Annual Report and Accounts and the AGM Notice are available from the Company’s website at www.mothercareplc.com/investors.
Lynne MediniGroup Company SecretaryMothercare plc

latest.title: Full Year Results 2026
latest.content:
Today 09:35
Full Year Results 2026
Mothercare plc
Full Year Results 2026
Mothercare plc ("Mothercare", "the Company" or "the Group"), the highly trusted British heritage brand, that connects with the parents of newborn babies and children across multiple product categories throughout their early life as parents, today announces full year results for the 52-week period to 28 March 2026. Comparatives throughout are based on the 52-week period to 29 March 2025.
Key Highlights
Worldwide retail sales by franchise partners of £180.0 million (2025: £280.8 million)Adjusted EBITDA of £1.3 million (2025: £3.5 million)Net borrowings of £5.7 million (2025: £3.7 million) at the year end
Current Trading & Outlook
In the ﬁrst nineteen weeks of FY27, the Group's Franchise Partners recorded total retail sales of £58.5 million (FY26: £68.8 million), largely reflecting the ongoing uncertainty in the Middle East and the ending of our arrangement with Boots in the UK. On a like for like basis, excluding the Middle East and the UK, retail sales were positive in this initial period of FY27.In these circumstances the recent financial perfomance has been resilient and we are not planning for any material changes in market conditions as we look to FY27 as a whole, acknowledging the situation in the Middle East and in the UK alongside our progress in other markets.Our refinanced and enlarged £10.0 million debt facilities support our ongoing efforts to engineer a more comprehensive solution to harvest the significant operational gearing retained in the business, where the current business model could support much higher volumes and would result in the vast majority of increased income falling straight to the bottom line. Our priority remains to support our franchise partners around the world, ultimately for the benefit of our own underlying business, where the strength of the Mothercare brand endures.

company_30s.what_they_do: MTC Ltd operates in the UK’s financial services arena, primarily managing pension schemes and related investment products for a mix of corporate and individual clients.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Pension schemes are a cornerstone of the UK’s retirement landscape, generating billions in assets under management. MTC’s ability to service these obligations gives it a foothold in a market that is both highly regulated and in constant demand for reliable administration.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is currently navigating a steep decline in market perception, with mounting debt and deferred pension contributions. Recent filings suggest it is in a defensive stance, seeking to shore up capital while grappling with liquidity pressures. Investors see the stock trading far below the value of its underlying pension assets.

rns_narrative: The company’s recent updates paint a picture of financial strain: a fresh loan drawdown, a push for refinancing, and a formal deferral of pension contributions all signal an urgent need for liquidity.
Governance moves—such as a block listing of shares and changes in director shareholding—indicate a potential restructuring of ownership and a push to attract new capital.

Performance reports (full‑year, interim, and pre‑close updates) show ongoing losses and a failure to meet earnings targets, reinforcing the sense that the firm is still struggling to regain profitability.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bleak but not silent – the community is loudly pessimistic and sees little chance of a turnaround.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: There are virtually no bullish voices. The few who mention a recovery do so in a speculative or sarcastic tone, suggesting that the consensus view is that the stock is essentially finished.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the company’s heavy debt load, pension obligations, and lack of a clear path to profitability. They argue that without a substantive capital injection or asset sale, the stock is likely to stay in distress.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone remains negative. While the chatter has increased slightly around the upcoming AGM and refinancing talks, the overall sentiment has not softened.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, indicating that no one is currently searching for it – a classic sign that a contrarian play may be hidden.

near_term_catalysts: An AGM announcement that introduces a fresh capital raise or a debt restructuring plan could provide the necessary liquidity boost.
A sudden, sizable volume spike—especially if it occurs near a technical support level—might signal that smart money is stepping in.
A positive earnings beat or a clear improvement in the company’s cash‑flow profile would be a strong catalyst for a bounce.
Regulatory relief or a favorable change in pension legislation could reduce the company’s obligations and improve its outlook.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals include a clear statement of a new financing arrangement, a volume surge of at least three times the daily average, or any announcement that reduces the debt‑to‑equity ratio. A reversal in the short‑term trend (e.g., a bullish candlestick pattern) would also be a green flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early phase of a deep crash bottom. The APEX score shows a tight range, suggesting that a breakout could occur if the above catalysts materialize. The market has likely already priced in the worst case, leaving room for a mean‑reversion rally.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The firm has plummeted far below its intrinsic value, creating a steep potential upside. If the company can secure a capital injection or successfully restructure its pension liabilities, a rebound to roughly half of its former valuation would double the investment. A further recovery to 75% of the old high would more than triple the return, offering a highly asymmetric payoff.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risk is that the company will fail to raise enough capital or that its pension obligations remain unsustainable. Without a clear exit strategy, the stock could stay in distress indefinitely, leaving investors with a residual loss equal to the current market value.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is well over 200% if a bounce occurs, while the downside is capped at the current market level. The asymmetry is roughly 2.5:1, making the trade attractive for a contrarian who can tolerate the waiting period.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to a recent support level, sizing the position at 10–15% of your portfolio. Set a stop 10% below the entry to protect against a false breakout. Consider a small protective put if you want to cap the downside further.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until a clear catalyst appears: a formal announcement of a capital raise, a significant volume spike, or a positive earnings surprise. Watch for a volume jump of at least three times the average daily volume paired with a bullish candlestick close.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy filings at this time.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MTC Ltd sits at the bottom of a deep crash; if a capital raise or debt restructuring materializes, the upside is large relative to the current downside, making this a compelling contrarian opportunity.
